research.interface: vSphere Automation API for vCenter (OpenAPI 3.0.3, info.version 9.0.0.0, server base path /api)
research.derivation: spec-derived: every field of docs/contract.json was read out of the OpenAPI document below, not out of a rendered documentation page

operations.used_for: the mutating call under test; carries the optional Client-Token request header whose spec text is 'Client-generated token used to retry a request if the client fails to get a response from the server. If the original request succeeded, the result of that request will be returned, otherwise the operation will be retried.' Request body is the required pair target (Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.DeploymentTarget) + deployment_spec (Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec); 200 body is Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.DeploymentResult

the read-back used to prove the retried deploy produced exactly one virtual machine; query parameter names is an array with style: form, explode: true, and the 200 body is a bare array of Vcenter.VM.Summary

research.language_rationale: VMware ships govmomi/govc, the vSphere client used across VCF tooling, in Go, and vCenter automation in VCF estates is overwhelmingly Go; this package speaks the documented /api REST surface with net/http only, so it drops into a CI image with no VMware SDK, and go test -race exercises the concurrent-deploy path a token ledger has to survive.

verified_facts: The 9.0.0.0 vcenter.yaml declares openapi 3.0.3, info.title 'vSphere Automation API', info.version '9.0.0.0', and a single server https://{host}/api — so every operation path in the document is served under the /api prefix.

The OpenAPI path key for the deploy operation embeds its query string: '/vcenter/ovf/library-item/{ovfLibraryItemId}?action=deploy'. The wire request is therefore POST /api/vcenter/ovf/library-item/{id}?action=deploy.

operationId Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem_deploy declares a header parameter named exactly 'Client-Token', in: header, required: false, type string, described as the client-generated token used to retry a request when the client fails to get a response; if the original request succeeded the result of that request is returned, otherwise the operation is retried. If the header is missing or null the server creates a token.
Four other operations in the same document reject a malformed token with the text 'if the clientToken does not conform to the UUID format', which fixes the token's required lexical form as a UUID.

The deploy request body is an inline object with required ['deployment_spec','target'] and exactly two properties, target -> Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.DeploymentTarget and deployment_spec -> Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec. Body property names are snake_case even though the path and header parameters are camelCase/Train-Case.

Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.DeploymentTarget requires only resource_pool_id; host_id and folder_id are optional and each documents 'If missing or null, the server will ...', so an unset value is expressed by omitting the property, never by an empty identifier string.

Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec requires only accept_all_eula (a boolean). accept_all_eula is therefore sent even when false, while name, annotation, network_mappings, storage_mappings, storage_provisioning, storage_profile_id, locale, flags, additional_parameters, default_datastore_id and vm_config_spec are optional and omitted when unset.

The 9.0.0.0 ResourcePoolDeploymentSpec has exactly twelve properties. The 9.1.0.0 revision of the same file (tag 9.1.0.0, commit 3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26) adds subnet_mappings and tag_params, which do not exist in 9.0.0.0 — a client pinned to 9.0.0.0 must never emit them.

The 200 response of the deploy operation is Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.DeploymentResult: required succeeded (boolean), optional resource_id (Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.DeployableIdentity with required type and id) and optional error (Vcenter.Ovf.LibraryItem.ResultInfo with required errors/warnings/information arrays). A deploy can therefore fail with HTTP 200 and succeeded=false.
Vcenter.Ovf.OvfError requires category (VALIDATION, INPUT or SERVER) and carries an optional localizable message; Vapi.Std.LocalizableMessage requires id, default_message and args.

Error responses use the vAPI envelope Vapi.Std.Errors.Error with required error_type (a discriminator string such as NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, UNAUTHENTICATED) and required messages, a stack of Vapi.Std.LocalizableMessage. The deploy operation documents 400 InvalidArgument, 403 Unauthorized, 404 NotFound and 500 ResourceInaccessible.

Vapi.Std.Errors.ServiceUnavailable allOf-extends Vapi.Std.Errors.Error and documents 'Attempt to invoke a operation when the server is too busy'; 503 'If the service is not available.' appears on 535 operations across the document, which is the documented transient condition a Client-Token retry is meant to cover.

The declared security scheme api_key_auth is type apiKey, in: header, name: vmware-api-session-id; the document also offers basic_auth and federated_identity_auth, but the deploy and list operations are secured with api_key_auth.

operationId Vcenter.VM_list is GET /vcenter/vm whose 'names' query parameter is a uniqueItems array of string with style: form and explode: true, so several names are sent as repeated names= pairs; the 200 body is a bare JSON array of Vcenter.VM.Summary (required vm, name, power_state; optional cpu_count and memory_size_mib), with no {"value": ...} envelope.

9.0.0.0 also defines a different, task-based deploy at path key '/vcenter/ovfs?action=deploy&vmw-task=true' with operationId Vcenter.Ovfs_deploy$Task, added in vSphere API 9.0.0.0. It takes no Client-Token header, so it is not the retry-safe operation this contract pins.
